correctness.rationale: Exact even/odd recursion reduces all dyadic block sums to two-letter sums. Alternating nonzero signs force all equal consecutive block sums to be zero. A Boolean indicator with alternating odd entries excludes four equal runs; valuation-class sign equidistribution and a parity-conditional adjacent-pair lemma give natural densities of 1/4 for squares and 1/16 for cubes and Parikh weights (1/4,1/2,1/4). The unit-period boundary is handled separately. The included program passed 3,154,986 integer assertions; finite tests supplement the stated infinite proof.

evidence: Holub 2012, Theorem 8, establishes arbitrary Abelian exponents with existence at unspecified suitable periods.
Fici–Postic–Silva 2018, Theorem 8, establishes Abelian antipowers for arbitrary folding instructions.
Burns 2022 treats factor appearance functions for arbitrary folding instructions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An existence statement quantified over unrestricted periods does not imply an exact exclusion when period \(2^k\) or a density law at those periods. Antipowers require distinct rather than equal Parikh vectors, and factor appearance is a different statistic. These broad results do not cover the claimed dyadic joint distribution.

evidence: The class count \(\rho(2^k)=3\) can be deduced from the present distribution but is already known for the ordinary folding word.
Holub establishes powers of every exponent over unrestricted periods; the present theorem shows that their periods cannot be dyadic when exponent≥4.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A statement on non-dyadic or unspecified periods cannot imply a dyadic exclusion. Knowing three classes exist does not specify their weights or temporal correlations. The new exact distribution entails a previously known restricted support result, which is explicitly credited; reverse implication is not established or warranted.

evidence: Holub 2012 defines Abelian powers through constant Parikh vectors and analyzes stratified interval counts.
Madill–Rampersad 2012 establishes class-count regularity, including three classes at powers of two.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The theorem was compared in equivalent language of equal block counts, signed block sums, balanced dyadic blocks, and runs in a parity-encoded sequence. Known dyadic Parikh-support cardinality alone neither fixes 1/4,1/2,1/4 probabilities nor consecutive-window correlations 1/4 and 1/16. No equivalent full statement was found in the inspected works.

evidence: Madill–Rampersad 2012 gives an exact class-count recurrence and \(\rho(2^k)=3\).
The relevant published work inspected did not contain the complete equal-Parikh run density table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The published known table concerns the number of possible Parikh classes, not their starting-position densities or the simultaneous equality of multiple adjacent dyadic blocks. The new frequencies are not presented as a rediscovery of the known support cardinality. Indexed searches are supporting negative evidence only.

originality.rationale: The newly proved theorem concerns every paperfolding instruction sequence, a complete dyadic-period Abelian power exponent cutoff, exact square/cube starting densities, and full Parikh frequencies. Primary text comparisons show that known all-exponent existence, dyadic support cardinality, appearance functions and anti-powers do not directly supply these joint distributions. An unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed equivalent theorem or a hidden implication from full general paperfolding factor-frequency machinery remains possible.
The known dyadic three-class support for the regular word is prior work and is not itself a new claim.

value.rationale: All paperfolding words have Abelian powers of arbitrarily high exponent at unrestricted periods, so exact exclusion of exponent four at every dyadic period is a nontrivial structural boundary. Exact square/cube occurrence densities and the complete Parikh distribution simultaneously cover infinitely many periods and every folding instruction sequence, strengthening the prior result that only counts possible classes.
